app.title: Artemis Kids
facilityDesc.habitat: A home for one crew member. Inside, its walls block some radiation.
facilityDesc.solar: Turns sunlight into electricity. In shadow it makes nothing!
facilityDesc.battery: Stores electricity so you still have power while the panels are in shadow.
facilityDesc.antenna: Talks to Earth, but only when Earth is above the horizon and in view.
facilityDesc.greenhouse: Crew grow food here with lights, water and power.
facilityDesc.lifeSupport: Uses electricity to turn ice and water into water and oxygen to breathe.
facilityDesc.iceDrill: Digs ice by itself. Only works in dark, frozen craters, uses lots of power and wears out fast.
facilityDesc.shield: A thick wall that blocks radiation for the whole base.
crewTaskDesc.maintenance: Fixes worn-out equipment using spare parts.
crewTaskDesc.research: Does science. Results count only after they are sent to Earth.
crewTaskDesc.farming: Grows food in the grow room.
hud.flareActive: Space weather storm! {hours} h left ({seconds} s at this speed)
pause.title: ⏸ Paused
pause.body: Time is stopped. Your oxygen tank is not going down.
repair.noParts: Not enough spare parts (this repair needs {need}, you have {have}). Order Spare parts with Supply.
build.title: Build
build.dustCoverDesc: Moon dust wears machines out. A cover slows that down, but costs extra materials and power.
build.materialPick: ↓ Choose what the wall is made of (pick one)
build.materialDesc.regolith: Regolith is moon dirt. It is free to dig, but takes time and materials to pile up.
build.materialDesc.water: Water blocks radiation better for the same thickness, but uses water you need to live.
build.good: Good spot: it will work here
placement.needsShadow: it must sit in a dark, frozen spot
placement.notEnoughMaterials: not enough materials → order Building materials from Earth (Supply)
placement.noSunlight: it is in shadow, so it won't make power now
placement.noEarth: Earth can't be seen from here
launch.title: Supply (order from Earth)
tutorial.step.buildHabitat.keys: Let's make a home for a new crew member. Use Build the same way and choose Habitat.
tutorial.step.buildHabitat.touch: Let's make a home for a new crew member. Use Build the same way and choose Habitat.
tutorial.why.buildHabitat: A Habitat is a home. Only one person can live in each. You live in the first one, so build another before you invite a crew member.
launch.notYet: You can order again in {days} days (use "Next day" to move ahead)
launchItemWhy.oxygen: For breathing. It also fills your tank when you go outside. A life support unit can make it from water.
launchItemWhy.water: For drinking. The life support unit uses it to make oxygen, and the greenhouse uses it to grow food. It can also become a water wall against radiation. Collecting ice adds more.
launchItemWhy.food: The crew eats it. The more people, the faster it runs out. A greenhouse can grow more.
launchItemWhy.spareParts: For fixing worn-out facilities, both when you repair them and when a crew member on maintenance does.
launchItemWhy.materials: Materials for building facilities. Used in "Build".
launchItemWhy.crew: More hands for research, maintenance and farming. But they also eat and breathe. Each person needs one habitat.
launchItemWhy.relaySatellite: Lets you talk to Earth even when Earth is below the horizon. One covers most of that time, two cover all of it. It still needs the base antenna and power.
crew.title: Crew
crew.beds: Crew {count} / room for {capacity} (one person per habitat)
crew.youDesc: You build, carry ice and repair by hand.
flare.explain.solarFlare: A solar flare is a giant flash on the Sun. It can send dangerous radiation all the way to the Moon.
flare.explain.sep: Solar energetic particles (SEP) are super-fast bits of the Sun. Thick walls and moon dirt help block them.
flare.archived: A real past event, recorded on {date} (archived data)
flare.sourceLink: See it in NASA's DONKI space weather database
flare.hint: Inside, walls block much of the radiation. Outside, your dose goes up fast.
flare.duration: ⏳ The storm ends in about {hours} h (about {seconds} s at the current speed)
flare.waitInside: 🏠 Wait inside: dose +{dose} mSv. Outdoor work pauses until then.
flare.stayOutside: 🚶 Stay outside: dose +{dose} mSv (now {now} / limit {limit} mSv)
flare.overLimit: ⚠️ Staying outside would take you over the limit and you would collapse!
flare.underLimit: It stays under the limit, but your dose never goes back down.
event.commLost: Lost contact with Earth. Warnings and orders can't get through.
downed.title: You passed out!
downed.wake: Because this is training, you woke up in the habitat. On a real mission this would be game over, so be careful!
cleared.title: Base complete!
cleared.body: Your development reached {value}. A new landing stage is unlocked!
cleared.next: 🔒 More south pole landing sites (coming soon)
death.cause.tankEmpty: Your tank ran out of oxygen while you were outside. You were {meters} m from a habitat.
death.cause.radiationStorm: You stayed outside during a solar storm and took too much radiation.
death.cause.radiationNoAlert: There was no contact with Earth, so the warning never reached you.
death.cause.oxygenNoLifeSupport: There was no Life Support unit to make oxygen. The oxygen from Earth was not enough.
death.cause.oxygenNoPower: The Life Support unit had stopped because there was not enough electricity.
death.cause.oxygenBroken: The Life Support unit was broken and had stopped.
death.cause.oxygenNoWater: Life Support makes oxygen from water, and there was not enough water.
death.cause.oxygenNotEnough: Everyone was breathing more oxygen than the base could make.
death.cause.waterNoSource: There was no way to get more water (carrying ice, or an Ice Drill).
death.cause.waterDrillNoPower: The Ice Drill had stopped because there was not enough electricity.
death.cause.waterDrillBroken: The Ice Drill was broken and had stopped.
death.cause.waterNotEnough: The base used water faster than it got more. The Greenhouse and Life Support use water too.
death.cause.foodNoGreenhouse: There was no Greenhouse to grow food.
death.cause.foodNoFarmer: There was a Greenhouse, but no crew member was set to Farming.
death.cause.foodNoPower: The Greenhouse had stopped because there was not enough electricity.
death.cause.foodBroken: The Greenhouse was broken and had stopped.
death.cause.foodNotEnough: Everyone was eating more food than the base could grow.
death.tip.tankHalf: When the Life bar is half empty, start heading back to a habitat.
death.tip.tankOutpost: For long trips, build a habitat along the way. Going inside any habitat fills your tank.
death.tip.shelter: When a warning comes, choose 'Go inside now'.
death.tip.stormTime: The warning and the top right show how long the storm lasts. Go outside after it ends.
death.tip.shield: Pile regolith on the habitat or build a Radiation Shield to make inside safer.
death.tip.commForAlerts: Warnings come from Earth. Power your antenna, and order Relay satellites so warnings always arrive.
death.tip.buildLifeSupport: Build a Life Support unit with Build.
death.tip.orderOxygen: If there is no time, order Oxygen with Supply.
death.tip.morePower: Add Solar Panels, and build Batteries for the dark times.
death.tip.repair: Set a crew member to Maintenance, or use Repair next to it. You need spare parts.
death.tip.getIce: Use Collect ice where there is ice, and carry it to a habitat.
death.tip.orderWater: If there is no time, order Water with Supply.
death.tip.moreLifeSupport: When your crew grows, add more Life Support units.
death.tip.buildIceDrill: Build an Ice Drill on ice to keep getting water.
death.tip.orderFood: If there is no time, order Food with Supply.
death.tip.assignFarmer: Use Crew to set someone to Farming.
death.tip.moreGreenhouse: When your crew grows, add more Greenhouses.
gameOver.title: Life support failed
gameOver.resumeFrom: Go back to a save and try again:
save.title: Save and resume
save.autoNote: Saves automatically each time you rest, and keeps the last {days} days.
data.title: Where the data comes from
data.spaceWeatherNote: The solar storms in this game are real past events, replayed from the archive. They are not live.
data.valuesPending: The sources for the game's numbers are still being checked.
data.terrain: The terrain is generated automatically for now. Real lunar terrain data is not used yet.
achievement.shelteredFromFlare: Took shelter from a solar flare
carry.ice: Carrying ice — bring it into a habitat to turn it into water
build.hint.mouse: Move the mouse to choose a spot, then click to build. Esc to cancel.
build.hint.touch: Tap the ground to choose a spot, then tap Place here.
tutorial.title: Training
tutorial.welcome.title: Welcome to the Moon base!
tutorial.welcome.question: Have you played this game before?
tutorial.finished.title: Training complete!
tutorial.finished.body: Now you can run the base yourself. Follow the missions to grow it. Your goal is Development 60!
tutorial.step.move.keys: Let's walk! HOLD DOWN the W A S D keys or the arrow keys (keep pressing) to walk.
tutorial.step.move.touch: Let's walk! Put your finger on the circle at the bottom left and slide it while holding.
tutorial.step.look.keys: Now look around! Drag on the screen with the mouse to turn the camera.
tutorial.step.look.touch: Now look around! Slide your finger on the screen to turn the camera.
tutorial.step.jump.keys: Press Space to jump. Gravity on the Moon is weak, so you float!
tutorial.step.jump.touch: Tap Jump. Gravity on the Moon is weak, so you float!
tutorial.step.buildSolar.keys: Let's make electricity! Press the glowing Build button (or B), then choose Solar Panel.
tutorial.step.buildSolar.touch: Let's make electricity! Tap the glowing Build button, then choose Solar Panel.
tutorial.step.placeSolar.keys: Move the mouse and a Solar Panel shape follows it. Click where the shape turns green to build. Yellow means shade, red means you can't build there.
tutorial.step.placeSolar.touch: Tap the ground and a Solar Panel shape appears. Pick a spot where it turns green, then tap 'Place here'. Yellow means shade, red means you can't build there.
tutorial.step.power.keys: Look at the glowing 'Power' at the top left. Green + is power made, red − is power used. If the bottom line shows ▲ power is going up, ▼ means down. If + is 0, the Solar Panel is resting in the shade.
tutorial.step.power.touch: Look at the glowing 'Power' at the top left. Green + is power made, red − is power used. If the bottom line shows ▲ power is going up, ▼ means down. If + is 0, the Solar Panel is resting in the shade.
tutorial.step.dictionary.keys: Press the glowing Word guide button to open it, then tap 'Solar Panel' to read about it. When you are done, press 'Back to the game'.
tutorial.step.dictionary.touch: Tap the glowing ❓ (Word guide) at the top right to open it, then tap 'Solar Panel' to read about it. When you are done, tap 'Back to the game'.
tutorial.step.battery.keys: Next, build a Battery the same way. It saves electricity for when the panels are in the shadow.
tutorial.step.battery.touch: Next, build a Battery the same way. It saves electricity for when the panels are in the shadow.
tutorial.timeStopped: ⏸ Time is stopped during training (take your time reading)
tutorial.goOutsideFirst: You are inside the habitat now. First press the glowing 'Go outside' button.
tutorial.step.commLost: Look at the top right. It says 'No contact with Earth' right now. {reason} When you can talk to Earth, orders and storm warnings get through.
tutorial.step.comm.keys: Look at the top right: 'Talking to Earth'. The antenna can talk to Earth only while Earth is above the horizon. You need it to order things and to get storm warnings.
tutorial.step.comm.touch: Look at the top right: 'Talking to Earth'. The antenna can talk to Earth only while Earth is above the horizon. You need it to order things and to get storm warnings.
tutorial.step.lifeLine.keys: Look at 'Life support: N days left' at the top left. It shows about how many days your oxygen, water and food will last right now. When it drops, make more or order from Earth.
tutorial.step.lifeLine.touch: Look at 'Life support: N days left' at the top left. It shows about how many days your oxygen, water and food will last right now. When it drops, make more or order from Earth.
tutorial.step.order.keys: Let's order from Earth! Press the glowing "Supply" step at the top (L key), add "Food" and "New crew member" with +, then press "Send order".
tutorial.step.order.touch: Let's order from Earth! Press the glowing "Supply" step at the top, add "Food" and "New crew member" with +, then press "Send order".
tutorial.step.waitArrival.keys: The rocket is still flying. Press "Next day" until it arrives.
tutorial.step.waitArrival.touch: The rocket is still flying. Press "Next day" until it arrives.
tutorial.step.assignCrew.keys: A new crew member arrived! Press the glowing "Crew" step at the top (C key) and choose "Farming" or "Maintenance".
tutorial.step.assignCrew.touch: A new crew member arrived! Press the glowing "Crew" step at the top and choose "Farming" or "Maintenance".
tutorial.step.toIce.keys: To make water, go get ice! Walk to the glowing pillar in a dark crater. Follow the arrow. Watch your suit oxygen bar.
tutorial.step.toIce.touch: To make water, go get ice! Walk to the glowing pillar in a dark crater. Follow the arrow. Watch your suit oxygen bar.
tutorial.step.takeIce.keys: You found ice! Press E (Collect ice) to pick it up.
tutorial.step.takeIce.touch: You found ice! Tap Collect ice to pick it up.
tutorial.step.goHome.keys: Carry the ice back to the glowing pillar at your habitat. Press E to go inside, and the ice turns into water.
tutorial.step.goHome.touch: Carry the ice back to the glowing pillar at your habitat. Tap Go inside, and the ice turns into water.
tutorial.step.flareDrill.keys: Training alarm! It uses a real solar flare record from 2024. Choose 'Go inside now' to stay safe.
tutorial.step.flareDrill.touch: Training alarm! It uses a real solar flare record from 2024. Choose 'Go inside now' to stay safe.
tutorial.step.flareDrillRetry: That's dangerous! In a real storm, go inside. Try again and choose 'Go inside now'.
tutorial.step.goOutside.keys: It is morning. Let's go outside. Press E ("Go outside").
tutorial.step.goOutside.touch: It is morning. Let's go outside. Press "Go outside".
tutorial.step.regolith.keys: Moon soil (regolith) blocks radiation. Next to the habitat, press the glowing 'Pile regolith on the habitat' button.
tutorial.step.regolith.touch: Moon soil (regolith) blocks radiation. Next to the habitat, press the glowing 'Pile regolith on the habitat' button.
tutorial.step.resume.keys: Time has stopped. When you are ready, press the glowing 'Resume' button to carry on.
tutorial.step.resume.touch: Time has stopped. When you are ready, press the glowing 'Resume' button to carry on.
tutorial.step.save.keys: Let's save the game. Press the glowing "Save" button at the top right, then press "Save here".
tutorial.step.save.touch: Let's save the game. Press the glowing "Save" button at the top right, then press "Save here".
tutorial.step.data.keys: Last one! Press the glowing Data button to see where the real NASA data in this game comes from.
tutorial.step.data.touch: Last one! Press the glowing Data button to see where the real NASA data in this game comes from.
mission.title: Mission
mission.allDone: All missions complete! Keep your crew safe and keep growing your base.
mission.lifeSupport: Build Life Support. It turns water into the oxygen your crew breathes.
mission.greenhouse: Grow food: build a Grow Room and give a crew member the Farming job. If you have no crew yet, order a New crew member with Supply.
mission.crew3: Grow your team to 3 crew members (order them from Earth). Each person needs one habitat.
mission.relay: Order a relay satellite with Supply so you can talk to Earth even when Earth is below the horizon.
mission.shield: Build a Radiation Shield wall to protect the whole base.
mission.complete: Raise Development to 60 and complete the base!
advice.tankLow.title: Your suit oxygen is running low!
advice.tankLow.todo:
1. Hurry back to the habitat (follow the arrow).
2. Go inside to refill your tank.
advice.oxygenLow.title: Oxygen is running out!
advice.oxygenLow.todo:
1. Build Life Support (it makes oxygen from water).
2. Order Oxygen from Earth.
advice.waterLow.title: Water is running out!
advice.waterLow.todo:
1. Carry ice from a dark crater to the habitat.
2. Build an Ice Drill in a dark crater.
3. Order Water from Earth.
advice.foodLow.title: Food is running out!
advice.foodLow.todo:
1. Order Food from Earth.
2. Build a Grow Room and give a crew member the Farming job.
advice.noPower.title: Not enough electricity! Some machines stopped.
advice.noPower.todo:
1. Build more Solar Panels in the sunlight.
2. Build a Battery to save electricity for the shadow.
3. Too many machines? Fewer machines use less power.
advice.broken.title: A machine is wearing out!
advice.broken.todo:
1. Walk to it (follow the arrow) and press E to repair it. It uses spare parts.
2. Give a crew member the Maintenance job to fix machines for you.
advice.noParts.title: No spare parts left!
advice.commLost.title: No contact with Earth.
advice.label: What to do
tutorial.why.move: You are an astronaut who just landed at the Moon's south pole. Your job: build a base where people can live.
tutorial.why.look: Look carefully: light and shadow, dark craters, and Earth in the sky. They are hints for where to build.
tutorial.why.jump: Gravity (the pull that makes things fall) on the Moon is much weaker than on Earth, so you feel very light.
tutorial.why.buildSolar: Every machine in the base runs on electricity, but there are no power plugs on the Moon. A Solar Panel turns sunlight into electricity.
tutorial.why.placeSolar: A solar panel only makes electricity in sunlight, so where you put it matters.
tutorial.why.power: Power means electricity. If you make more than you use, everything keeps working.
tutorial.why.dictionary: Special words used in space and at the base collect in the Word guide. If you forget one, open it any time and read it again.
tutorial.why.battery: At the south pole the Sun moves low around the sky, so shadows are long and move. A Battery is a box that stores electricity for the shadow time.
tutorial.why.comm: The antenna (the pole with a dish, already next to your base) talks to Earth. You need it to order (ask for) things and to get warnings (messages that say "danger!"). When Earth sinks below the horizon (where the sky meets the ground), you cannot talk.
tutorial.why.lifeLine: Everyone needs the base's oxygen, water and food to live. If even one of them runs out, the game is over.
tutorial.why.order: Things you cannot make on the Moon come from Earth by rocket. But one rocket can only carry so much.
tutorial.why.waitArrival: A rocket takes three days to reach the Moon. To wait, move the days forward with "Next day".
tutorial.why.assignCrew: Crew members are your teammates. Farming means growing food; Maintenance means fixing broken machines.
tutorial.why.toIce: The Moon has no rivers or rain. But at the bottom of dark craters that never get sunlight, there is ice. Melted ice becomes water.
tutorial.why.takeIce: The tank on the back of your space suit holds the oxygen you breathe. If it runs out, you pass out and the game is over. Get back before it runs out.
tutorial.why.goHome: The habitat is the home where everyone lives. Inside, your oxygen tank fills up again.
tutorial.why.flareDrill: A solar flare is a huge explosion on the Sun. It sends radiation (invisible, dangerous light and particles) all the way to the Moon. Taking too much outside makes you pass out, and the game is over. Building walls protect you.
tutorial.why.goOutside: When the storm is over, you can work outside again.
tutorial.why.regolith: Regolith is the sand and rocks of the Moon. Piled on your home, it works like a thick wall that blocks radiation.
tutorial.why.pause: Pause stops time. While paused, the oxygen in your tank does not go down. Use it when you want to think things over, or when you step away for a meal or the bathroom.
tutorial.why.resume: While paused, you cannot walk or build.
tutorial.why.save: Saving records your base as it is now. Save before something hard, like a long trip for ice, so you can try again from there if it goes wrong (it also saves automatically each time you go inside).
tutorial.why.data: The solar flares in this game use real records that NASA collected.
tutorial.step.goInsideWait.keys: The new home is ready. Outside work is done for today. Go next to the habitat and press E to go inside.
tutorial.step.goInsideWait.touch: The new home is ready. Outside work is done for today. Go next to the habitat and press "Go inside".
tutorial.why.goInsideWait: Your tank oxygen does not last long. Going inside ends your outside work for the day. Time stops inside, so you can plan your base slowly.
commHint.noPower: → The antenna has no electricity. Build Solar Panels (and a Battery).
commHint.earthDown: → Earth is below the horizon. Wait until it rises, or order a Relay satellite while you can talk.
commHint.blocked: → The antenna cannot see Earth (a hill is in the way). Build an antenna where Earth is visible.
launch.noLinkChain.noPower: To send an order you must talk to Earth → the antenna has no electricity → build Solar Panels (Build).
launch.noLinkChain.earthDown: To send an order you must talk to Earth → Earth is below the horizon now → wait until it rises (a Relay satellite lets you talk any time).
launch.noLinkChain.blocked: To send an order you must talk to Earth → the antenna cannot see Earth → build an Antenna where Earth is visible.
launch.noLinkChain.noAntenna: To send an order you must talk to Earth → there is no antenna → build an Antenna (Build).
hud.tankIndoors: Inside: you breathe the base air, so it is safe.

help.label: Word guide
help.title: Word guide
help.term.solar.name: Solar Panel
help.term.solar.what: A panel that turns sunlight into electricity.
help.term.solar.why: Every machine runs on electricity. In shadow it makes nothing, so put it in the sunlight.
help.term.battery.name: Battery
help.term.battery.why: At the south pole the Sun is low and shadows move. A battery keeps machines running in the shadow.
help.term.power.name: Power (+ made / − used)
help.term.power.what: Electricity. + is what you make, − is what you use.
help.term.power.why: If − is bigger than +, the battery runs down and machines stop.
help.term.lifeSupport.name: Life Support
help.term.lifeSupport.what: A machine that makes the oxygen we breathe from water, using electricity.
help.term.lifeSupport.why: Without it, the base oxygen keeps going down.
help.term.habitat.name: Habitat
help.term.habitat.what: A home where the crew live. One person per habitat.
help.term.habitat.why: Inside, the walls block radiation and your suit tank refills.
help.term.tank.name: Suit oxygen tank
help.term.tank.what: The oxygen on the back of your space suit. Your "life" outside.
help.term.tank.why: If it runs out you pass out. Come back inside before it gets low.
help.term.ice.name: Ice and permanent shadow
help.term.ice.what: Some dark craters never get sunlight. Ice stays frozen at the bottom.
help.term.ice.why: Melted ice becomes water. Water is also used to make oxygen.
help.term.iceDrill.name: Ice Drill
help.term.iceDrill.what: A machine that digs ice by itself. It only works in dark, frozen places.
help.term.iceDrill.why: You no longer have to carry ice by hand, but it uses lots of electricity.
help.term.greenhouse.name: Grow Room
help.term.greenhouse.what: A room where crew grow food with light, water and electricity.
help.term.greenhouse.why: Growing food on the Moon means you need fewer rockets from Earth.
help.term.radiation.name: Radiation
help.term.radiation.what: Invisible, dangerous light and tiny particles from space and the Sun.
help.term.radiation.why: The Moon has no air to block it, so walls and soil protect you.
help.term.flare.name: Solar flare
help.term.flare.what: A huge explosion on the surface of the Sun.
help.term.flare.why: Strong ones send lots of radiation. When the warning comes, go inside.
help.term.sep.name: SEP (solar energetic particles)
help.term.sep.what: Super-fast particles shot out by the Sun.
help.term.sep.why: Thick walls and moon soil help block them.
help.term.dose.name: Dose (mSv)
help.term.dose.what: How much radiation your body has taken. mSv is its unit.
help.term.dose.why: Too much is bad for your body. Stay inside during storms.
help.term.shield.name: Radiation Shield wall
help.term.shield.what: A thick wall that blocks radiation for the whole base.
help.term.shield.why: Water walls block better, but use water you need to live.
help.term.regolith.name: Regolith
help.term.regolith.what: The sand and rocks covering the Moon.
help.term.regolith.why: Piled on your home, it works like a thick wall against radiation.
help.term.materials.name: Materials
help.term.materials.what: The stuff used to build facilities.
help.term.materials.why: If you run out, order Building materials from Earth.
help.term.repair.name: Maintenance and spare parts
help.term.repair.what: Fixing worn-out machines. It uses spare parts.
help.term.repair.why: Moon dust wears machines out. Broken machines stop working.
help.term.launch.name: Supply
help.term.launch.what: Getting what you need sent from Earth by rocket.
help.term.launch.why: One rocket can only carry so much, so choose what matters most.
help.term.antenna.name: Antenna
help.term.antenna.what: A machine for talking to Earth.
help.term.antenna.why: You need it to order things and to get storm warnings. It needs electricity, even if you have Relay satellites. A second antenna in another spot where Earth is visible is a good backup if one breaks.
help.term.horizon.name: Horizon
help.term.horizon.what: Where the sky meets the ground.
help.term.horizon.why: When Earth sinks below it, you cannot talk to Earth.
help.term.relay.name: Relay satellite
help.term.relay.what: A satellite that passes your messages on to Earth. Talking to it still needs your base's antenna and electricity.
help.term.relay.why: With it you can talk even when Earth is below the horizon.
help.term.development.name: Development and the four stars
help.term.development.what: How good your base is now: self-sufficiency, stability, safety and scale.
help.term.development.why: Reach 60 to complete the base. Leaving it alone does not raise it.
help.term.research.name: Research
help.term.research.what: Science work done by crew. It counts only after it is sent to Earth.
help.term.research.why: It grows your base. Keep in touch with Earth to send it.
help.term.donki.name: DONKI
help.term.donki.what: NASA's record of real space weather, such as solar flares.
help.term.donki.why: The solar flares in this game are real past events from it.
morning.title: Morning of day {day}
morning.lead: While you slept, this happened at the base.
morning.spaceWeather.solarFlare: A solar flare ({cls}, a real past event) happened while you slept. You were inside, so the base protected you from radiation.
morning.spaceWeather.sep: A solar particle storm (SEP, {cls}, a real past event) happened while you slept. You were inside, so the base protected you from radiation.
rest.reason.eva: A spacesuit tank only holds {hours} hours of oxygen.
rest.reason.sleep: Astronauts sleep {hours} hours every day, too.
rest.reason.weekly: Astronauts work outside only about {hours} hours a week. Going out tired makes injuries more likely.
rest.next: Outside work is done for today. Press "Next day" to go to tomorrow.
eva.warn: {minutes} minutes of tank oxygen left (game time)! Head back to the habitat.
tutorial.step.nextDay.keys: Press the glowing "Next day" to sleep. Time moves on until morning.
tutorial.step.nextDay.touch: Press the glowing "Next day" to sleep. Time moves on until morning.
tutorial.why.nextDay: Time stops while you are inside, so you can think slowly. When you press "Next day", the crew works while you sleep, and supplies get used.
tutorial.step.arrived.keys: It arrived! Look at the supplies that came in, in the morning window. Then press "Let's go!".
tutorial.step.arrived.touch: It arrived! Look at the supplies that came in, in the morning window. Then press "Let's go!".
tutorial.why.arrived: The morning window shows what went up and down while you slept. Check it every morning.
notebook.title: Inside the habitat · Day {day}
research.title: Research
research.body: The crew studies the science of the Moon.
research.note: Research only counts toward development once it reaches Earth. Choose who does research on the next page, "Crew".
review.title: Today's review
review.morning: It is morning. You have not gone outside yet.
review.did.ice: Carried ice and turned it into water
tasks.title: Choose tomorrow's tasks
tasks.lead: You can stay outside for {hours} hours (tank oxygen). You may not finish everything, so pick the important ones first.
plan.title: Tomorrow's plan
plan.empty: No tasks chosen yet. Choose them in "Tomorrow's tasks".
plan.goOutNote: When you are ready, press "Go outside". A beam of light will guide you to each task.
plan.sleepNote: Press "Next day" and time moves on while you sleep.
minigame.failed: Time is up! You lost some of your time outside.
inventory.title: Base details
tutorial.step.inventory.keys: Press the glowing "Details" (I key). You can see the numbers for life support, power and supplies here. Close it with ✕ when you are done.
tutorial.step.inventory.touch: Press the glowing "Details". You can see the numbers for life support, power and supplies here. Close it with ✕ when you are done.
tutorial.why.inventory: The outside screen only shows the most important number: your tank. The other numbers are gathered in "Details". Time stops while it is open.
tutorial.step.chooseTask.keys: In "Tomorrow's tasks" at the top, choose "Dig and carry ice". Then head out with "Go outside".
tutorial.step.chooseTask.touch: In "Tomorrow's tasks" at the top, choose "Dig and carry ice". Then head out with "Go outside".
tutorial.why.chooseTask: Your time outside is limited and you cannot do everything, so decide first what to do. Outside, a beam of light guides you to the next place.
tutorial.step.sleepAgain.keys: That is all for today. Sleep with "Next day" and start tomorrow.
tutorial.step.sleepAgain.touch: That is all for today. Sleep with "Next day" and start tomorrow.
tutorial.why.sleepAgain: You can go outside once a day. Rest, then go out again tomorrow.
cards.title: Fact cards
cards.got: 🃏 You got a card: "{title}" (read it inside)
card.regolith.title: Why is Moon dust (regolith) a problem?
card.regolith.body: Moon dust is very fine and sticks to spacesuits. When scientists studied the Apollo 12 spacesuits, they found the grains had split and frayed the threads of the fabric. That is why astronauts need ways to keep dust out when they come back inside.
card.regolith.hint: How to get it: cover a habitat with regolith
card.radiation.title: Space radiation and how to stay safe
card.radiation.body: Earth is protected by its magnetic field and its air. The Moon has neither, so solar flares are dangerous for astronauts and machines. When an alert comes, get inside behind walls.
card.radiation.hint: How to get it: take shelter during a solar flare alert
card.evaHours.title: How long can you stay outside in a spacesuit?
card.evaHours.body: In the Artemis program, one outside work session on the Moon is planned to last about 6 to 8 hours. Spacesuit oxygen is limited too, so watch the time and come back.
card.evaHours.hint: How to get it: come back to the habitat after working outside
notebook.inOrder: Go step by step with "Next" at the bottom.
notebook.buildOutside: Building is done outside. Go outside, then press "Build".
